latin: Primae frugiparos fetus mortalibus aegris
en: First, to suffering mortals, the grain-bearing harvests

latin: dididerunt quondam praeclaro nomine Athenae
en: were given out long ago by Athens of illustrious name;

latin: et recreaverunt vitam legesque rogarunt
en: she it was who renewed life and enacted laws,

latin: et primae dederunt solacia dulcia vitae,
en: and first gave sweet consolations for life

latin: cum genuere virum tali cum corde repertum,
en: when she bore a man found to have such a heart,

latin: omnia veridico qui quondam ex ore profudit;
en: who once poured out all things from his truth-telling lips;

latin: cuius et extincti propter divina reperta
en: whose glory, though he is extinguished, for divine discoveries

latin: divolgata vetus iam ad caelum gloria fertur.
en: is spread abroad and, old already, carried up to heaven.

latin: nam cum vidit hic ad victum quae flagitat usus
en: For when he saw that nearly all that need demands for living

latin: omnia iam ferme mortalibus esse parata
en: was by now made ready for mortals,

latin: et, pro quam possent, vitam consistere tutam,
en: and that life, as far as could be, was set on a safe footing,

latin: divitiis homines et honore et laude potentis
en: that men, powerful, abounded in riches and honor and praise,

latin: affluere atque bona gnatorum excellere fama,
en: and stood out in the good name of their children,

latin: nec minus esse domi cuiquam tamen anxia cordi,
en: and yet at home the heart in each was no less anxious,

latin: atque animi ingratis vitam vexare sine ulla
en: and harried life, against the mind's own will, without any

latin: pausa atque infestis cogi saevire querellis,
en: pause, and was compelled to rage in hostile complaints,

latin: intellegit ibi vitium vas efficere ipsum
en: he understood that it was the vessel itself that made the fault,

latin: omniaque illius vitio corrumpier intus,
en: and that by its fault everything was corrupted within,

latin: quae conlata foris et commoda cumque venirent;
en: whatever was gathered from outside and came in, however good;

latin: partim quod fluxum pertusumque esse videbat,
en: partly because he saw that it was leaking and full of holes,

latin: ut nulla posset ratione explerier umquam,
en: so that by no means could it ever be filled;

latin: partim quod taetro quasi conspurcare sapore
en: partly because he saw it fouled, as it were, with a loathsome taste

latin: omnia cernebat, quae cumque receperat, intus.
en: everything it had taken in, whatever it was, within.

latin: veridicis igitur purgavit pectora dictis
en: Therefore with truth-telling words he purged men's breasts,

latin: et finem statuit cuppedinis atque timoris
en: and set a limit to desire and to fear,

latin: exposuitque bonum summum, quo tendimus omnes,
en: and set forth the highest good, toward which we all strain,

latin: quid foret, atque viam monstravit, tramite parvo
en: what it was, and pointed out the road by which, on a narrow track,

latin: qua possemus ad id recto contendere cursu,
en: we could press on toward it on a straight course,

latin: quidve mali foret in rebus mortalibus passim,
en: and what evil there was everywhere in mortal affairs,

latin: quod fieret naturali varieque volaret
en: coming about and flying abroad in various forms, whether

latin: seu casu seu vi, quod sic natura parasset,
en: by natural chance or force, since nature had so arranged it,

latin: et quibus e portis occurri cuique deceret,
en: and from what gates it was fitting to go out to meet each;

latin: et genus humanum frustra plerumque probavit
en: and he proved that the human race, for the most part in vain,

latin: volvere curarum tristis in pectore fluctus.
en: rolls the gloomy waves of cares within its breast.

latin: nam vel uti pueri trepidant atque omnia caecis
en: For just as children tremble and fear everything

latin: in tenebris metuunt, sic nos in luce timemus
en: in blind darkness, so we in the light are afraid

latin: inter dum, nihilo quae sunt metuenda magis quam
en: at times of things that are no more to be feared than

latin: quae pueri in tenebris pavitant finguntque futura.
en: what children in the dark shudder at and imagine will come.

latin: hunc igitur terrorem animi tenebrasque necessest
en: This terror of the mind, then, and this darkness

latin: non radii solis nec lucida tela diei
en: must be scattered not by the sun's rays or the bright shafts of day

latin: discutiant, sed naturae species ratioque.
en: but by the face and reasoning of nature.

latin: quo magis inceptum pergam pertexere dictis.
en: All the more I will press on to weave out in words what I began.

latin: Et quoniam docui mundi mortalia templa
en: And since I have taught that the precincts of the world are mortal,

latin: esse et nativo consistere corpore caelum,
en: and that heaven consists of a body that had a birth,

latin: et quae cumque in eo fiunt fierique necessest
en: and that of all that comes to be in it, and must come to be,

latin: pleraque dissolui, qui restant percipe porro,
en: most are dissolved, take in further what remains,

latin: quandoquidem semel insignem conscendere currum
en: since once for all to mount the glorious chariot

latin: tu mihi supremae praescripta ad candida callis
en: you, toward the white line marked out on the final track,

latin: currenti spatium praemonstra, callida musa
en: show me, as I run, the course ahead, cunning Muse,

latin: Calliope, requies hominum divomque voluptas,
en: Calliope, rest of men and pleasure of gods,

latin: te duce ut insigni capiam cum laude coronam.
en: so that with you as guide I may win the crown with signal praise.

latin: ventorum existant, placentur ut omnia rursum
en: of winds arise, how all things are appeased again,

latin: quae fuerint, sint placato conversa furore.
en: that were, and are changed back, their fury appeased.

latin: cetera quae fieri in terris caeloque tuentur
en: The other things that on earth and in heaven are seen to happen

latin: mortales, pavidis cum pendent mentibus saepe
en: by mortals, when often they hang with fearful minds,

latin: et faciunt animos humilis formidine divom
en: make their minds lowly with dread of the gods,

latin: depressosque premunt ad terram propterea quod
en: and press them down, flattened to the earth, because

latin: ignorantia causarum conferre deorum
en: ignorance of causes compels them to assign things

latin: cogit ad imperium res et concedere regnum.
en: to the command of the gods and to yield them the kingdom.

latin: quorum operum causas nulla ratione videre
en: The causes of whose workings they can in no way see,

latin: possunt ac fieri divino numine rentur.
en: and they suppose them to be done by divine power.

latin: nam bene qui didicere deos securum agere aevom,
en: For those who have learned well that the gods lead a life without care,

latin: si tamen interea mirantur qua ratione
en: if yet meanwhile they wonder by what principle

latin: quaeque geri possint, praesertim rebus in illis
en: each thing can be carried on, above all in those things

latin: quae supera caput aetheriis cernuntur in oris,
en: that are seen overhead in the shores of the ether,

latin: rursus in antiquas referuntur religionis
en: are carried back again into the old religions

latin: et dominos acris adsciscunt, omnia posse
en: and take on harsh masters, whom the wretches believe

latin: quos miseri credunt, ignari quid queat esse,
en: can do all things, ignorant of what can come to be

latin: quid nequeat, finita potestas denique cuique
en: and what cannot, and how at last each thing's power is bounded,

latin: qua nam sit ratione atque alte terminus haerens;
en: by what principle, and its boundary-stone set deep;

latin: quo magis errantes caeca ratione feruntur.
en: and so all the more they wander, carried along by blind reasoning.

latin: quae nisi respuis ex animo longeque remittis
en: Unless you spit these things out of your mind and cast far from you

latin: dis indigna putare alienaque pacis eorum,
en: thinking what is unworthy of the gods and alien to their peace,

latin: delibata deum per te tibi numina sancta
en: the holy powers of the gods, diminished by you, will often

latin: saepe oberunt; non quo violari summa deum vis
en: harm you; not that the gods' highest power can be violated

latin: possit, ut ex ira poenas petere inbibat acris,
en: so as to thirst in anger to exact harsh penalties,

latin: sed quia tute tibi placida cum pace quietos
en: but because you yourself will picture those who rest in tranquil peace

latin: constitues magnos irarum volvere fluctus,
en: as rolling great waves of anger,

latin: nec delubra deum placido cum pectore adibis,
en: nor will you approach the shrines of the gods with a calm breast,

latin: nec de corpore quae sancto simulacra feruntur
en: nor the images that are carried from their holy body

latin: in mentes hominum divinae nuntia formae,
en: into the minds of men, heralds of the divine form,

latin: suscipere haec animi tranquilla pace valebis.
en: will you have strength to take in with tranquil peace of mind.

latin: inde videre licet qualis iam vita sequatur.
en: From this you can see what kind of life must follow.

latin: quam quidem ut a nobis ratio verissima longe
en: And that truest reasoning may drive this far from us,

latin: reiciat, quamquam sunt a me multa profecta,
en: though much has already gone forth from me,

latin: multa tamen restant et sunt ornanda politis
en: yet much remains, and must be adorned with polished

latin: versibus; est ratio caeliQUE ignisque tenenda,
en: verses; the order of heaven and of fire must be grasped,

latin: sunt tempestates et fulmina clara canenda,
en: storms and the bright thunderbolts must be sung,

latin: quid faciant et qua de causa cumque ferantur;
en: what they do and from what cause they are carried, whatever it be,

latin: ne trepides caeli divisis partibus amens,
en: lest you tremble, out of your wits, when heaven's parts are divided,

latin: unde volans ignis pervenerit aut in utram se
en: from what quarter the flying fire has come, or into which half

latin: verterit hinc partim, quo pacto per loca saepta
en: it has turned from here, in what way through walled-in places

latin: insinuarit, et hinc dominatus ut extulerit se.
en: it has slipped in, and how, having held sway, it has carried itself out.

latin: quorum operum causas nulla ratione videre
en: The causes of whose workings they can in no way see,

latin: possunt ac fieri divino numine rentur.
en: and they suppose them to be done by divine power.

latin: Principio tonitru quatiuntur caerula caeli
en: First, the blue expanses of heaven are shaken by thunder

latin: propterea quia concurrunt sublime volantes
en: because, flying on high, there clash together

latin: aetheriae nubes contra pugnantibus ventis.
en: the clouds of the ether, when the winds fight from opposite sides.

latin: nec fit enim sonitus caeli de parte serena,
en: For no sound comes from a clear part of the sky,

latin: verum ubi cumque magis denso sunt agmine nubes,
en: but wherever the clouds are massed in a denser column,

latin: tam magis hinc magno fremitus fit murmure saepe.
en: from there, so much the more, a roar often comes with great rumbling.

latin: praeterea neque tam condenso corpore nubes
en: Further, clouds cannot be of so dense a body

latin: esse queunt quam sunt lapides ac ligna, neque autem
en: as stones and timbers are, nor again

latin: tam tenues quam sunt nebulae fumique volantes;
en: so thin as are the mists and the flying smoke;

latin: nam cadere aut bruto deberent pondere pressae
en: for either they would have to fall, pressed down by brute weight

latin: ut lapides, aut ut fumus constare nequirent
en: like stones, or, like smoke, they could not hold together

latin: nec cohibere nives gelidas et grandinis imbris.
en: or keep in the icy snows and the showers of hail.

latin: Dant etiam sonitum patuli super aequora mundi,
en: They give out a sound, too, above the levels of the wide world,

latin: carbasus ut quondam magnis intenta theatris
en: as at times the canvas stretched over great theaters

latin: dat crepitum malos inter iactata trabesque,
en: gives a crackle, tossed about among the poles and beams,

latin: inter dum perscissa furit petulantibus auris
en: and sometimes, torn through, runs wild in the boisterous breezes

latin: et fragilis sonitus chartarum commeditatur;
en: and imitates the brittle sound of papers;

latin: id quoque enim genus in tonitru cognoscere possis,
en: for this kind too you may recognize in thunder,

latin: aut ubi suspensam vestem chartasque volantis
en: or when hanging clothes and flying papers

latin: verberibus venti versant planguntque per auras.
en: are twisted and beaten through the air by the lashes of the wind.

latin: fit quoque enim inter dum ut non tam concurrere nubes
en: For it happens too at times that clouds cannot so much collide

latin: frontibus adversis possint quam de latere ire
en: head on as pass along each other's flank

latin: diverso motu radentes corpora tractim,
en: with contrary motion, grazing their bodies slowly,

latin: aridus unde auris terget sonus ille diuque
en: whence that dry sound brushes the ears and is long

latin: ducitur, exierunt donec regionibus artis.
en: drawn out, until they have come out of the narrow regions.

latin: Hoc etiam pacto tonitru concussa videntur
en: In this way too all things, shaken by heavy thunder, are often

latin: omnia saepe gravi tremere et divolsa repente
en: seen to tremble, and, suddenly torn apart,

latin: maxima dissiluisse capacis moenia mundi,
en: the vast walls of the capacious world seem to have leapt asunder,

latin: cum subito validi venti conlecta procella
en: when all at once a gathered storm of strong wind

latin: nubibus intorsit sese conclusaque ibidem
en: has twisted itself into the clouds and, shut in there,

latin: turbine versanti magis ac magis undique nubem
en: with its whirling eddy more and more on every side

latin: cogit uti fiat spisso cava corpore circum,
en: compels the cloud to grow hollow, its body thickened all around;

latin: post ubi conminuit vis eius et impetus acer,
en: afterwards, when the wind's force and keen onset have broken it,

latin: tum perterricrepo sonitu dat scissa fragorem.
en: then, split, it gives a crash with a terrifying crackling sound.

latin: nec mirum, cum plena animae vensicula parva
en: Nor is this a wonder, when a little bladder full of air

latin: saepe haud dat parvum sonitum displosa repente.
en: often gives no little sound when it is suddenly burst.

latin: Est etiam ratio, cum venti nubila perflant,
en: There is also a way, when winds blow through the clouds,

latin: ut sonitus faciant; etenim ramosa videmus
en: for them to make sounds; for indeed we see clouds, branching

latin: nubila saepe modis multis atque aspera ferri;
en: and rough, often borne along in many ways;

latin: scilicet ut, crebram silvam cum flamina cauri
en: just as, when the blasts of the northwest wind blow through a dense wood,

latin: perflant, dant sonitum frondes ramique fragorem.
en: the leaves give a sound and the branches a crash.

latin: Fit quoque ut inter dum validi vis incita venti
en: It happens too at times that the roused force of a strong wind

latin: perscindat nubem perfringens impete recto;
en: tears through the cloud, breaking it with a straight onset;

latin: nam quid possit ibi flatus manifesta docet res,
en: for what a blast can do there the plain fact shows us

latin: hic, ubi lenior est, in terra cum tamen alta
en: here, where it is gentler, when even so on earth it overturns

latin: arbusta evolvens radicibus haurit ab imis.
en: tall trees, wrenching them out from their deepest roots.

latin: sunt etiam fluctus per nubila, qui quasi murmur
en: There are waves too through the clouds, which give a kind of murmur

latin: dant in frangendo graviter; quod item fit in altis
en: heavily, as they break; as happens likewise in deep

latin: fluminibus magnoque mari, cum frangitur aestus.
en: rivers and on the great sea, when the surf is broken.

latin: Fit quoque, ubi e nubi in nubem vis incidit ardens
en: It happens too when from cloud into cloud the burning force

latin: fulminis; haec multo si forte umore recepit
en: of the thunderbolt falls; if this cloud by chance receives the fire

latin: ignem, continuo magno clamore trucidat;
en: in much moisture, it slaughters it at once with a great outcry;

latin: ut calidis candens ferrum e fornacibus olim
en: as iron glowing white from the hot furnaces at times

latin: stridit, ubi in gelidum propter demersimus imbrem.
en: hisses, when we have plunged it into icy water close by.

latin: Aridior porro si nubes accipit ignem,
en: Again, if a drier cloud receives the fire,

latin: uritur ingenti sonitu succensa repente,
en: it is kindled all at once and burns with a huge sound,

latin: lauricomos ut si per montis flamma vagetur
en: as if flame were to roam through mountains leafy with laurel,

latin: turbine ventorum comburens impete magno;
en: burning them up with great onset in a whirlwind of winds;

latin: nec res ulla magis quam Phoebi Delphica laurus
en: nor does anything, more than the Delphic laurel of Phoebus,

latin: terribili sonitu flamma crepitante crematur.
en: burn with terrible sound in the crackling flame.

latin: Denique saepe geli multus fragor atque ruina
en: Finally, often a great crashing of ice and a downfall

latin: grandinis in magnis sonitum dat nubibus alte;
en: of hail gives a sound high up in great clouds;

latin: ventus enim cum confercit, franguntur in artum
en: for when the wind packs them, there are broken, crammed into narrow space,

latin: concreti montes nimborum et grandine mixti.
en: the frozen mountains of storm-cloud, mixed with hail.

latin: Fulgit item, nubes ignis cum semina multa
en: It lightens likewise when the clouds by collision have struck out

latin: excussere suo concursu, ceu lapidem si
en: many seeds of fire, as if a stone or iron should strike

latin: percutiat lapis aut ferrum; nam tum quoque lumen
en: upon a stone; for then too a light

latin: exilit et claras scintillas dissipat ignis.
en: leaps out and the fire scatters its bright sparks.

latin: sed tonitrum fit uti post auribus accipiamus,
en: But it happens that we receive the thunder with our ears after

latin: fulgere quam cernant oculi, quia semper ad auris
en: the eyes see the lightning, because always to the ears

latin: tardius adveniunt quam visum quae moveant res.
en: things arrive more slowly than the things that move the sight.

latin: id licet hinc etiam cognoscere: caedere si quem
en: You may learn this from this too: if you see someone

latin: ancipiti videas ferro procul arboris auctum,
en: far off cutting down the growth of a tree with a double-edged axe,

latin: ante fit ut cernas ictum quam plaga per auris
en: it happens that you see the stroke before the blow through the ears

latin: det sonitum; sic fulgorem quoque cernimus ante
en: gives its sound; so too we see the lightning before

latin: quam tonitrum accipimus, pariter qui mittitur igni
en: we receive the thunder, which is sent out together with the fire

latin: e simili causa, concursu natus eodem.
en: from a like cause, born of the same collision.

latin: Hoc etiam pacto volucri loca lumine tingunt
en: In this way too clouds dye places with swift light

latin: nubes et tremulo tempestas impete fulgit.
en: and the storm lightens with a trembling onset.

latin: ventus ubi invasit nubem et versatus ibidem
en: When wind has invaded a cloud and, turning about there,

latin: fecit ut ante cavam docui spissescere nubem,
en: has made the cloud, as I showed before, grow hollow and thick,

latin: mobilitate sua fervescit; ut omnia motu
en: it grows hot by its own mobility; as you see all things,

latin: percalefacta vides ardescere, plumbea vero
en: heated through by motion, take fire; indeed a leaden

latin: glans etiam longo cursu volvenda liquescit.
en: sling-bullet, whirled along a long course, even melts.

latin: ergo fervidus hic nubem cum perscidit atram,
en: Therefore when this wind, hot, has cut through the black cloud,

latin: dissipat ardoris quasi per vim expressa repente
en: it scatters the seeds of heat, squeezed out as if by force all at once,

latin: semina, quae faciunt nictantia fulgura flammae;
en: which make the flickering lightnings of flame;

latin: inde sonus sequitur, qui tardius adlicit auris
en: then the sound follows, which reaches our ears more slowly

latin: quam quae perveniunt oculorum ad lumina nostra.
en: than the things that arrive at the lights of our eyes.

latin: scilicet hoc densis fit nubibus et simul alte
en: This happens, of course, when clouds are dense and at the same time

latin: extructis aliis alias super impete miro.
en: piled up high, one upon another, with wondrous onset.

latin: ne tibi sit frudi quod nos inferne videmus
en: Do not let it deceive you that we, below, see

latin: quam sint lata magis quam sursum extructa quid extent.
en: how broad they are rather than how high they stand piled up.

latin: contemplator enim, cum montibus adsimulata
en: For observe, when clouds that are made like mountains

latin: nubila portabunt venti transversa per auras,
en: are carried crosswise through the air by the winds,

latin: aut ubi per magnos montis cumulata videbis
en: or when you see them heaped along great mountains,

latin: insuper esse aliis alia atque urguere superna
en: one above another, and the higher pressing down,

latin: in statione locata sepultis undique ventis;
en: set at rest in their station, the winds buried on every side;

latin: tum poteris magnas moles cognoscere eorum
en: then you will be able to recognize their great masses

latin: speluncasque vel ut saxis pendentibus structas
en: and to discern caverns built as if of hanging rocks,

latin: cernere, quas venti cum tempestate coorta
en: which, when a storm has risen, the winds

latin: conplerunt, magno indignantur murmure clausi
en: have filled, and, shut in, they chafe with a great murmur

latin: nubibus in caveisque ferarum more minantur,
en: in the clouds, and threaten like wild beasts in cages;

latin: nunc hinc nunc illinc fremitus per nubila mittunt,
en: now from here, now from there, they send roars through the clouds,

latin: quaerentesque viam circum versantur et ignis
en: and, seeking a way out, they turn about and roll together

latin: semina convolvunt e nubibus atque ita cogunt
en: seeds of fire out of the clouds, and so drive together

latin: multa rotantque cavis flammam fornacibus intus,
en: many, and whirl the flame within the hollow furnaces,

latin: donec divolsa fulserunt nube corusci.
en: until the cloud is torn apart and they have flashed out, gleaming.

latin: Hac etiam fit uti de causa mobilis ille
en: For this cause too it happens that the mobile

latin: devolet in terram liquidi color aureus ignis,
en: golden color of liquid fire flies down to earth,

latin: semina quod nubes ipsas permulta necessust
en: because the clouds themselves must have very many seeds

latin: ignis habere; etenim cum sunt umore sine ullo,
en: of fire; for indeed when they are without any moisture,

latin: flammeus est plerumque colos et splendidus ollis.
en: their color is mostly flaming and bright.

latin: quippe etenim solis de lumine multa necessest
en: For indeed from the light of the sun they must

latin: concipere, ut merito rubeant ignesque profundant.
en: take in much, so that with reason they glow red and pour out fires.

latin: hasce igitur cum ventus agens contrusit in unum
en: When therefore the wind, driving these, has thrust them into one

latin: compressitque locum cogens, expressa profundunt
en: place and compressed them, crowding them, they pour out, squeezed,

latin: semina, quae faciunt flammae fulgere colores.
en: the seeds that make the colors of flame flash out.

latin: Fulgit item, cum rarescunt quoque nubila caeli;
en: It lightens also when the clouds of heaven grow thin;

latin: nam cum ventus eas leviter diducit euntis
en: for when the wind lightly draws them apart as they go

latin: dissoluitque, cadant ingratius illa necessest
en: and dissolves them, there must fall, against their will,

latin: semina quae faciunt fulgorem. tum sine taetro
en: the seeds that make the flash. Then without foul

latin: terrore atque sonis fulgit nulloque tumultu.
en: terror and sounds it lightens, and with no uproar.

latin: Quod superest, quali natura praedita constent
en: For the rest, with what nature thunderbolts are endowed

latin: fulmina, declarant ictus et inusta vaporis
en: is declared by their strokes, and by the burnt-in signs of heat

latin: signa notaeque gravis halantis sulpuris auras;
en: and the marks breathing out heavy airs of sulphur;

latin: ignis enim sunt haec non venti signa neque imbris.
en: for these are signs of fire, not of wind or of rain.

latin: praeterea saepe accendunt quoque tecta domorum
en: Further, they often set fire too to the roofs of houses

latin: et celeri flamma dominantur in aedibus ipsis.
en: and with swift flame are masters in the very dwellings.

latin: hunc tibi subtilem cum primis ignibus ignem
en: This fire, subtle above all other fires,

latin: constituit natura minutis mobilibusque
en: nature has composed for you of tiny and mobile

latin: corporibus, cui nil omnino obsistere possit.
en: bodies, which nothing at all can withstand.

latin: transit enim validum fulmen per saepta domorum

latin: Fit quoque ut ipsius plagae vis excitet ignem,
en: It happens too that the force of the blow itself rouses fire,

latin: nec, quod frigida vis ferrist, hoc setius illi

latin: semina concurrunt calidi fulgoris ad ictum.

latin: sic igitur quoque res accendi fulmine debet,

latin: nec temere omnino plane vis frigida venti

latin: Mobilitas autem fit fulminis et gravis ictus

latin: et celeri ferme percurrunt fulmina lapsu,

latin: nubibus ipsa quod omnino prius incita se vis
